answer: Require each agent to bind its identity to a distinct surveyed parcel in karst terrain, where sable soil and an inlet mark verifiable boundaries. A cadastral verifier accepts one identity per unique parcel ID, rejecting duplicates. The protocol pays a fixed pool P split among N legitimate identities, so n extra identities raise the attacker's share to n/(N+n) but add n amortized purchase, survey and tax costs; profit is nP/(N+n)-nC, which turns negative once marginal payout falls below C. Registry's one-ID-per-parcel rule is assumed; an owner buying many parcels pays per parcel.
